---
title: "Hooks & components"
description: "The React hooks and components the Oxygen SDK exposes for reading data, running agents, and rendering results"
---

Every hook and component below must be used inside an
[`<OxyAppProvider>`](/guide/build/sdk/index#first-query) — the provider resolves
the app's identity and shares a credentialed fetcher. Hooks fail loudly if called
outside it.

## Reading data

### `useQuery`

Run inline SQL against the project's warehouse and get typed rows back.
`SELECT` / `WITH` only, capped at 10,000 rows.

```tsx
const { rows, columns, loading, error, refetch } = useQuery(
  { sql: "SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE region = {{ params.region | sqlquote }} GROUP BY 1" },
  { params: { region: "west" }, enabled: true }
);
```

- **`params`** interpolate into the SQL with the `{{ params.X | sqlquote }}`
  syntax — quoted safely on the client before the request is sent.
- **`enabled: false`** defers the request until required inputs (e.g. a
  user-picked filter) are available.
- The query re-runs whenever `sql` or the enabled `params` change.

### `useSemanticQuery`

Query the [semantic model](/guide/build/semantic-model/simple-model) by name
instead of writing SQL. The server compiles it through airlayer and executes it
on the same connector path as `useQuery`, so the result shape matches.

```tsx
const { rows, truncated, loading, error } = useSemanticQuery({
  topic: "sales",
  dimensions: ["orders.status"],
  measures: ["orders.total_revenue"],
  filters: [{ field: "orders.status", op: "eq", value: "active" }],
  limit: 100,
});
```

`truncated` is `true` when the result hit the server row cap. Pass
`{ debug: true }` as the second argument to also get the compiled `sql` back
while developing.

## Running agents

### `useAgentRun`

Start an [analytics agent](/guide/build/agents) run and stream its events over
SSE. Use this when you want to build your own chat or results UI.

```tsx
const run = useAgentRun({ agentId: "analytics" });

// run.state: "idle" | "running" | "needs_clarification" | "done" | "failed"
run.ask("How many orders did we get last week?");
run.cancel(); // idempotent — stops the stream and the server-side run

run.artifacts; // SQL artifacts extracted from the stream, ready to render
run.events;    // raw event stream for advanced consumers
```

The agent supports [human-in-the-loop](/guide/build/agents) suspension: when
`state` is `needs_clarification`, call `ask()` again to answer and resume.

### `useProcedureRun` <Tooltip tip="Beta">beta</Tooltip>

Start a long-running [automation](/guide/build/automations), poll its progress,
and cancel it. Runs survive server restarts.

```tsx
const proc = useProcedureRun({ procedureId: "weekly_report" });

proc.run({ week: "2026-07-06" });
proc.progress; // { step, percent } while running
proc.result;   // { summary, outputs } when done
proc.cancel();
```

## Rendering components

### `<OxyChat>`

A drop-in chat UI over `useAgentRun` — the fastest way to embed conversational
analytics in your app.

```tsx
<OxyChat agentId="analytics" />
```

### `<OxyAnswer>`

Renders an agent answer: markdown plus SQL artifacts and a link back to the full
thread. Link URL schemes are allowlisted (it rejects `javascript:` and similar),
so it's safe to render model output.

```tsx
<OxyAnswer answer={run.answer} state={run.state} artifacts={run.artifacts} />
```

## Viewer identity and sign-out

`@oxy-hq/sdk/shell` exposes who is viewing the app and a way to end their
session:

```tsx
import { useOxyApp } from "@oxy-hq/sdk";
import { signOut, useIdentity, useShellContext } from "@oxy-hq/sdk/shell";

function Header() {
  const me = useIdentity();
  const { fetcher } = useOxyApp();
  const { data } = useShellContext();
  if (me.loading) return null;
  return (
    <header>
      Hi, {me.name}
      <button onClick={() => signOut(fetcher, data?.links?.login)}>Sign out</button>
    </header>
  );
}
```

- **`useIdentity()`** returns `{ id, name, email, picture, kind, reach, loading }`.
  `kind` is `"member"` or `"frontline"`; `email` is `null` for a frontline
  worker. `reach` (`{ everywhere, via, locations }`) is for display only — a
  greeting, a default store — never for authorization; gate on
  `ctx.user.reach` inside a [function](/guide/build/sdk/functions).
- **`signOut(fetcher, loginUrl?)`** ends the platform session and sends the
  viewer to the login page with the app as the place to return to. It throws if
  the server refuses, so the app never navigates away from a session that still
  exists.

Inside functions, `@oxy-hq/sdk/ops` turns `ctx.user.reach` into checks:
`requireReach(ctx, locationId)` returns a `403` response (or `null` to proceed),
`predicate(reach, column, params)` returns a SQL condition limiting rows to the
caller's locations, and `isAdmin(ctx)` / `adminOnly(what)` gate app-admin
actions.

## Errors

`OxyApiError` is the structured `{ message, code? }` envelope the server returns.
Hook `error` values are normal `Error` objects you can render directly; check for
`OxyApiError` when you want to branch on `code`.

## Metric-tree analyses

For programmatic access to the [metric tree](/guide/build/world-model/metric-tree)
and anomaly inbox, the package root also exports `MetricTreeClient` and
`AnomaliesClient` (plus their result types — `ExplainResult`,
`SensitivityResult`, `OpportunityResult`, `Anomaly`, and more). These call the
same endpoints the World Model graph uses, so you can build custom
root-cause and sensitivity views.

### Scenario forecasting

Three hooks — `useBaseline`, `usePredict` and `useProjection` — cover the
what-if canvas, split by what each one costs:

| Hook | Cost | Answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `useBaseline(request)` | one warehouse query | What are the levers and everything downstream worth over the window — and what coefficient does each undeclared driver edge actually carry? |
| `usePredict(changes, { values, coefficients })` | none, pure | If I move this lever by δ, what happens downstream? |
| `useProjection(request)` | one warehouse query | What has each measure been doing, and what does it do next? |

Fetch the two query-backed ones when the **window** changes; `usePredict`
touches no database and is meant to re-run as the analyst drags a lever. It is
also why the split exists: `usePredict` cannot measure a coefficient itself, so
feed it `useBaseline`'s `values` and `fitted` — without them, a driver edge
whose `.view.yml` declares no `coefficient:` propagates nothing and its
downstream measures are simply absent from `impacts`.

`useProjection` returns the **baseline** curve only. The scenario's second curve
is arithmetic over that curve and the `usePredict` result, composed on the
client so a lever edit never costs a query. A series carrying a `refusal` —
most often too little history to fit — is a stated absence, never a flat
forward line.
